sentences.text: Its skin was covered in tooth-like dermal denticles.
The pectoral fins sat about 14 cm from the head tip and extended just 5.2 cm along the body while projecting 2.5 cm outward.
John E. Harris proposed that Diademodus had a scavenging lifestyle based on its small teeth.
However, Harris suggested Diademodus hydei was piscivorous because bony fish scales were found in the stomach region of a fossil.
This creature lived during the Late Devonian Period.
Fossils have been found in Utah, Nevada, Western Australia, and Russia.
Michał Ginter suggested in 2008 that Diademodus utahensis may have had weakly attached teeth, limiting its ability to capture large prey.
